title: Chicken Mandi
tagline: Fragrant saffron rice and chicken finished with a signature charcoal smoke (dukhan).
intro: Mandi — of Hadhrami-Yemeni origin and now one of the most beloved dishes across Saudi Arabia — is defined by its gentle spicing and its unmistakable smokiness. Traditionally the meat is slow-cooked in an underground taboon oven; at home the magic comes from the dukhan technique, where a piece of glowing charcoal is drizzled with ghee inside the sealed pot to perfume the rice. The result is subtle, aromatic and deeply comforting.

items: 2 tbsp mandi spice mix (black pepper, cumin, coriander, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, turmeric)
500 g (2½ cups) basmati rice, soaked 30 min
Pinch of saffron soaked in 3 tbsp warm water
1 cinnamon stick, 4 cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 bay leaf

method: Rub the chicken with the mandi spices, salt and oil.
Make a broth: simmer the chicken in water with a little salt until just cooked, about 25 minutes. Reserve about 1 litre of broth; keep the chicken.
Roast or grill the spiced chicken at high heat until browned and tender.
Cook the drained rice in the measured broth with saffron and whole spices: boil, then cover and cook low 15 minutes.
Make a well in the cooked rice and sit the chicken on top (or a small heatproof bowl in the centre).
Dukhan: heat the charcoal until red-hot, place it in the bowl, drizzle the ghee over it so it smokes, and immediately cover the pot tightly. Leave sealed for 5–10 minutes.
Remove the charcoal, garnish with fried nuts and raisins and serve.
tips: The dukhan smoke is what makes mandi taste like mandi — don't skip it, and keep the lid tightly sealed.
Mandi spicing is milder than kabsa; let the saffron and smoke lead.
toServe: Serve with sahawiq (Yemeni green chilli sauce) or daqoos.
imageAlt: Chicken mandi with smoky saffron rice and roasted chicken
